title: Semilinear Frobenius transport and explicit field-operation lifts
statement:
Fix primes $p\ne\ell$, $a\ge1$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, an algebraic closure $k$ of $k_0$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in a fixed algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, and $\Lambda\in\{E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. For a finite-type $k_0$-scheme $T_0$ put $T=T_0\times_{k_0}k$, $g_T=\operatorname{id}_{T_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\operatorname{Frob}_q)$ with geometric Frobenius, and $P_T=Lg_T^*$ [def-weil-frobenius-detailed, def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Use the rational/common-stage bounded constructible categories and Weil pairs $(K,\theta_K:P_TK\xrightarrow{\sim}K)$, whose arrows satisfy $u\theta_K=\theta_LP_T(u)$ [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a separated finite-type morphism of finite-type $k_0$-schemes, and put $f=f_0\times_{k_0}k:X\to Y$. The square $fg_X=g_Yf$ is Cartesian as a square of schemes; to view it over $k$, its source corners have structural maps $a_Tg_T$. The functors $P_T$ are exact equivalences, inverse to pullback along $g_T^{-1}$, on these field coefficient categories. Their integral realization is the exact inverse-image transport on completed coefficient modules; the inverse-composition identities survive scalar localization and the common-finite-field construction.

For each covariant operation $F\in\{Lf^*,Rf_*,Rf_!\}$ on a domain where the underlying functor preserves bounded constructibility, let $a:P_{\mathrm{out}}F\xrightarrow{\sim}FP_{\mathrm{in}}$ be its canonical Frobenius comparison. The rule
$$ (K,\theta_K)\longmapsto(FK,F(\theta_K)a_K),\qquad u\longmapsto F(u) $$
is a functor on Weil pairs, and on Weil arrows it satisfies
$$ F(u)F(\theta_K)a_K=F(\theta_L)a_LP_{\mathrm{out}}(F(u)). $$
Here $Rf_!$ is the compact-support functor of [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed], with its field-coefficient passage as specified in [def-exchange-projection], and $Rf_*$ is [def-weil-derived-direct-image]. In particular $a=\operatorname{Ex}_*$ or $\operatorname{Ex}_!$ gives the specified direct-image structure. For $W=X,Y$, the tensor and internal-Hom structures are respectively
$$ (\theta_M\otimes\theta_N)\mu_g,\qquad R\mathcal Hom(\theta_M^{-1},\theta_N)h_g, $$
where $\mu_g:P_W(M\otimes^LN)\simeq P_WM\otimes^LP_WN$ and $h_g:P_WR\mathcal Hom(M,N)\simeq R\mathcal Hom(P_WM,P_WN)$ are the canonical transport comparisons. These formulas define functors, covariant in both tensor arguments and contravariant in the first Hom argument, on each already-proved constructible domain. In particular retain $M\in D^b_{ctf}$, $N\in D^b_c$ and any site-perfect first-variable restriction [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude, def-weil-site-perfect-complex]. Forgetting recovers the given objects and arrows of all five operations. Exactness is that of their underlying derived functors; this asserts neither larger constructibility domains nor a triangulated structure on Weil pairs.

source.place: Proof sentence 1: semilinear Frobenius square, exact rational transport, and explicit operation/evaluation lifts; returned proof Steps 1–2.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-frobenius-square-cartesian], $g_X,g_Y$ are scheme isomorphisms, $fg_X=g_Yf$, and the displayed square is Cartesian. This does not assert $k$-linearity. Indeed, if $a_T:T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is the usual structure map, the upper copy of $T$ has structure map $a_Tg_T$; then $g_T$ is a map to the lower copy over $k$, and $a_Yg_Yf=a_Xg_X$ makes the left vertical arrow a map over $k$. These are precisely the restructured source corners in the assertion.

For each $T$, [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image] gives the exact inverse-image equivalence on module sheaves, its inverse, and its compatibility with the completed coefficient sheaf (inverse image commutes with the inverse limit of constant coefficient sheaves). [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback] identifies the completed constructible pullback with this termwise transport, $\lambda^{g_T}_K:P_TK\xrightarrow{\sim}g_T^{-1}K$, and asserts that it preserves $D^b_c$. Apply the same result to $\bar g_T=g_T^{-1}$. Put $\epsilon_K:L\bar g_T^*P_TK\xrightarrow{\sim}K$ equal to $\lambda^{\bar g_T}_{P_TK}$, followed by $\bar g_T^{-1}(\lambda^{g_T}_K)$ and the canonical isomorphism of inverse images along $g_T\circ\bar g_T=\mathrm{id}$; define the other composite symmetrically with $g_T$ and $\bar g_T$ exchanged. These are natural isomorphisms, since $\lambda$ is natural and the inverse images are inverse site equivalences, so the two pullbacks are inverse equivalences on the integral constructible categories. Exactness follows already on module sheaves, hence also after passage to complexes and quasi-isomorphisms.

At $E$, use the raw scalar localization of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]: the integral functors $P_T$ and $L\bar g_T^*$ act on $\operatorname{Hom}(-,-)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$ by $u\otimes c\mapsto P_T(u)\otimes c$, so the inverse-identity isomorphisms of Step 2 stay natural for every $u\otimes c$ by linearity and each inverse identity remains the same equality after tensoring. At $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] represents every object and arrow over a common finite field, and the pullbacks act on an arrow represented over $L$ by its stage-$L$ image conjugated by the rationalized pullback scalar-extension comparisons $\alpha$ of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension]; these are natural, unital and compatible with successive extension, so the action does not depend on the representative. At $(E,K)$ take the class of the stage-$E$ isomorphism $\epsilon_K$ of Step 2. By [lem-pod-pullback-identities-scalar-extension] (2), the scalar extension of $\epsilon^E_K$ is $\epsilon^L$ at the extended object composed with exactly the two comparisons $\alpha$ by which the composite functor $L\bar g_T^*P_T$ acts on arrows over $L$. Hence for an arrow represented over $L$ the naturality square of these classes is the stage-$L$ naturality square of $\epsilon^L$ conjugated by those comparisons, and so commutes; tower compatibility makes the class independent of the representing field. Applying the same clause to $\bar g_T$ gives the other inverse identity. These identities therefore hold in the common-stage category too. This also preserves the exact structures, whose triangles are images of integral triangles or are represented over a common finite field.

source.place: Sentence 1, rationalization and common finite coefficient stages

proof.text: For $F=Lf^*$, form $a:P_XLf^*\xrightarrow{\sim}Lf^*P_Y$ as $c_{f,g_Y}\circ c_{g_X,f}^{-1}$ through $L(fg_X)^*=L(g_Yf)^*$, where $c_{h,k}:L(kh)^*\xrightarrow{\sim}Lh^*Lk^*$. At the integral stage these are the natural isomorphisms $c^{\mathcal O_E}_{h,k}$ of [lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition], which apply to arbitrary morphisms of schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible and whose reductions modulo $\varpi_E^n$ are the finite composition isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]; thus $a^{-1}$ is the square identification $\theta$ from which [def-exchange-projection] builds $\operatorname{Ex}_*$. At $E$, $a\otimes1$ is natural for every $u\otimes c$ by linearity. At $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ take at $(E,K)$ the class of the stage-$E$ component. By [lem-pod-pullback-identities-scalar-extension] (1), applied to the pairs $(g_X,f)$ and $(f,g_Y)$, the scalar extension of $c^{\mathcal O_E}$ is $c^{\mathcal O_L}$ conjugated by the composite comparisons $\alpha$ of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension], which are exactly the comparisons by which $P_XLf^*$ and $Lf^*P_Y$ act on arrows over $L$. So the classes are natural for arrows represented over any common field and independent of the representing field. Hence $a$ is a natural isomorphism of the specified pullbacks at both field stages.

For $F=Rf_*$ use $Lf^*\dashv Rf_*$ from [fix-prop-adjunctions] (1). With $L=L'=Lf^*$, $R=R'=Rf_*$, $G=P_Y$, $G'=P_X$, the inverse of the comparison in Step 4 has type $L'G\xrightarrow{\sim}G'L$. Its mate is exactly $\operatorname{Ex}_*$ in [def-exchange-projection], since that definition is the unit--pullback-comparison--counit composite. By [lem-weil-mate-iso-along-equivalences] it is invertible: Step 3 gives that $G$ is an equivalence and $G'$ is fully faithful. For $F=Rf_!$, [lem-pod-weil-frobenius-compact-support-exchange] gives the canonical natural isomorphism $\operatorname{Ex}_!$ at both field stages on the stated domains, without separatedness of either base scheme. Thus all three covariant comparisons $a$ are natural isomorphisms.

source.place: Sentence 1, ordinary and compact-support direct-image comparisons

proof.text:
Let $F$ be any of the three functors with its comparison $a$, and set $\Theta_K=F(\theta_K)a_K$. Both factors are invertible. If $u\theta_K=\theta_LP_{\mathrm{in}}(u)$, functoriality and naturality give
$$F(u)\Theta_K=F(u\theta_K)a_K=F(\theta_L)F(P_{\mathrm{in}}u)a_K=F(\theta_L)a_LP_{\mathrm{out}}(F(u)).$$
This is exactly the arrow condition in [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Identities and composition are preserved because the underlying arrows are $F(u)$; equality of arrows of pairs is equality of underlying arrows. Hence this gives the asserted three functors, including the specified direct-image formulas.

source.place: Sentence 1, explicit covariant lift and arrow calculation

proof.text:
For tensor use the natural isomorphism $\mu_g$ of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso] at the field stages and put $\Theta_{M,N}=(\theta_M\otimes\theta_N)\mu_{M,N}$. It is invertible. For Weil arrows $u:M\to M'$ and $v:N\to N'$, bifunctoriality, their two arrow equations, and naturality of $\mu$ give
$$(u\otimes v)\Theta_{M,N}=(u\theta_M\otimes v\theta_N)\mu_{M,N}=(\theta_{M'}\otimes\theta_{N'})(P_Wu\otimes P_Wv)\mu_{M,N}=\Theta_{M',N'}P_W(u\otimes v).$$
Tensor preserves identities and simultaneous composition, so the same holds for its lift. This calculation uses only the natural tensor comparison and its defining bifunctor; it makes no additional preservation assertion.

source.place: Sentence 1, tensor lift and its two-variable arrow calculation

proof.text:
Write $H=R\mathcal Hom$. [lem-pod-derived-automorphism-hom-evaluation] supplies the canonical natural isomorphism $h_{M,N}:P_WH(M,N)\xrightarrow{\sim}H(P_WM,P_WN)$ for an arbitrary scheme isomorphism, with the completed integral realization and its localized/common-stage forms, on pairs whose internal Hom is constructible. Set $\Theta_{M,N}=H(\theta_M^{-1},\theta_N)h_{M,N}$, an isomorphism. For arrows $u:M'\to M$, $v:N\to N'$ of Weil pairs, their equations imply $\theta_M^{-1}u=(P_Wu)\theta_{M'}^{-1}$ and $v\theta_N=\theta_{N'}P_Wv$. Contravariant/covariant functoriality and naturality of $h$ give
$$H(u,v)\Theta_{M,N}=H(\theta_M^{-1}u,v\theta_N)h_{M,N}=H(\theta_{M'}^{-1},\theta_{N'})H(P_Wu,P_Wv)h_{M,N}=\Theta_{M',N'}P_W(H(u,v)).$$
Thus $H(u,v)$ is a Weil arrow. Its identity and composition laws are the laws of the internal-Hom bifunctor in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. The inverse in the first input is essential: it has type $M\to P_WM$, precisely the contravariant input required for a map $H(P_WM,P_WN)\to H(M,N)$.

source.place: Sentence 1, internal-Hom lift, inverse first-variable datum and arrow calculation

proof.text: All constructions above leave each underlying object and arrow equal to the value of the stipulated operation. The forgetful functor of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex] therefore recovers all five operations. We have restricted throughout to the existing preserved constructible domains; tensor and Hom keep the finite-Tor and any site-perfect first-variable restrictions stated in the item. The formulas introduce no change to any underlying derived functor, shift comparison or underlying triangle. Thus their exactness means exactly the exactness already available for those underlying derived functors (in each covariant variable, and contravariantly in the first Hom variable); it supplies no triangulated-category claim about the category of pairs.
